reports.title: KIRBY CORPORATION ANNOUNCES THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS

guidance.heading: 2026 Outlook
section: Commenting on the outlook for the fourth quarter of 2026, Mr. Grzebinski stated, “As we enter the fourth quarter of 2026, we remain encouraged by the momentum across our businesses. Driven by strong operational execution and favorable market conditions, we believe Kirby is well positioned to capitalize on opportunities across our end markets and deliver solid performance in the remainder of the year. Despite ongoing macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty, customer demand remains healthy across many of our end markets. Based on current market conditions, we are narrowing our full-year earnings per share growth guidance to 10% to 15% and currently expect results toward the upper end of the range.”

In inland marine, market fundamentals are expected to remain constructive, supported by robust supply-demand dynamics and strong refinery and petrochemical operating rates. Barge utilization is expected to remain in the low-90% range, while both spot pricing and term contract renewal rates are expected to improve further during the remainder of the year. Inland operating conditions are expected to reflect normal seasonal weather impacts during the fourth quarter. Overall, inland revenues are expected to grow in the low-double-digit range, with operating margins expected to be in the high-teens to low-20% range for the full year.

In coastal marine, customer demand remains stable with barge utilization expected to remain in the high-90% range. Overall market conditions remain constructive, and pricing trends continue to improve, although elevated planned shipyard activity and higher fuel costs are expected to pressure margins during the fourth quarter. Overall, revenues are expected to increase in the mid-to-high-single-digit range for the full year, with operating margins expected to be in the mid-teens range.

In distribution and services, continued growth in power generation and strong marine repair activity are expected to support full-year results. In power generation, order momentum remains strong, supported by data center demand and the need for behind-the-meter and backup power solutions. While OEM engine delivery timing continues to create some variability in quarterly results, underlying customer demand remains robust. In commercial and industrial, customer activity is expected to remain healthy driven by strong demand in marine repair. In oil and gas, activity is expected to remain stable, subject to changes in the market environment. Overall, the Company expects segment revenues to grow in the high-single-digit range for the full year, with operating margins in the high-single-digit range.
